report.summary: One test fails: test_book_can_be_updated. It sends year=2001 in the PUT but asserts the stored year is 2002. The app stores exactly what it receives, so the test's expected value is wrong. Fix the test by making the expected year match the sent year (2001) or sending 2002, not by changing the app.

causes.title: Test sends year 2001 but expects 2002 after update
causes.explanation: The test PUTs year=2001 (line 23), then expects the GET to return year=2002 (line 27). The app's PUT handler writes the submitted year unchanged to the database and returns it, so the GET correctly returns 2001. The assertion's expected value is a typo or stale constant. Nothing in the app adds or transforms the year, so the application behaves correctly and the test is wrong.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:23: updated = api.update_book(book["id"], title="Final title", author="Someone", year=2001)
app/main.py:209-218: api_update_book runs UPDATE books SET title=?, author=?, year=? with book.year unchanged and returns {"id": book_id, **book.model_dump()}
app/main.py:143-144: book_dict returns row["year"] as stored, with no offset applied
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/api/test_books_api.py, change the expected "year" on line 27 to 2001 so it matches the value sent on line 23. Alternatively, change the sent year on line 23 to 2002 if that was the intent. Use a single constant for both values so they cannot drift apart again.
